components.name: accordion
components.title: Accordion
components.purpose: A set of disclosures of which one is open at a time, built on details elements that share a name.
whenToUse: For three or more sections of detail about one thing, such as the environment, commands and test output of a run, when the reader wants one at a time and the set should stay short.
When each section's summary can say in a few words what it holds.
whenNotToUse: When the reader compares sections or needs two open together. Use separate disclosures, which open and close alone.
For one section. Use a disclosure.
For panels that are the main content of a view. Use tabs.
For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical inside a closed section fails the hidden-critical-action rule.
Nested more than two levels. A disclosure inside a section is the limit, and a third level fails the disclosure-depth rule.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Each summary is at least 44px tall and as wide as the set, with a rule between sections and above and below the set.

accessibility: The set is a div with the gw-accordion class. Each section is a details element with the classes gw-disclosure and gw-accordion__section, a gw-disclosure__summary as its first child and one gw-disclosure__content after it. Copy the inside of a section from the disclosure component.

Give every section of one set the same name attribute, and a name no other set on the page uses. The browser then closes the open section when another opens. Where the name attribute is not supported the sections open and close alone, and nothing is lost.
At most one section carries the open attribute in the markup. The open attribute is the only state: never toggle a class.
Every summary holds text that says what the section holds. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule. Trailing text such as a count goes in a gw-disclosure__meta span.

Tab reaches each summary in order. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order, and the browser's find-in-page opens the section that holds a match.
Opening a section closes another without the reader asking, so keep nothing in a section that the reader is filling in, such as a half-written form.
A section may hold one more level of disclosure, a plain gw-disclosure with no name. Do not nest an accordion in an accordion.
The component needs no script.

components.name: activity-feed
components.title: Activity feed
components.purpose: A chronological record of what agents and people did, grouped by day, each entry with its time, its actor, a verb phrase and an optional source or excerpt.
whenToUse: For the history of a task, a run or a repository, read from the oldest entry shown to the newest.
When each event fits one line: who did what, and when.
With role="log" when entries are added while the reader watches.
whenNotToUse: For the full exchange with an agent, with prompts, tool output and answers. Use a transcript of messages.
For one tool call with its arguments and output. Use a tool call.
For a list of runs or tasks to open. Use a list with run status rows.
For a message about the app itself. Use an alert or a banner.
accessibility: Use a section with an aria-label that names what the activity belongs to, such as Activity for task 41. Each label is unique in the view.
Inside it, each day is a div with the class gw-activity-feed__day: a heading, at the level the view needs, that names the day in words such as Today, 22 November, then an ol of entries, oldest first.

An entry is an li holding a time element with a datetime attribute, then a p with the actor in gw-activity-feed__actor followed by a verb phrase that names the thing acted on, then optionally one gw-activity-feed__evidence holding a source chip or a short gw-activity-feed__excerpt.

When entries are appended while the reader watches, put role="log" on the section. A log is announced politely, entry by entry, and needs no script beyond adding the li. Keep role="log" off a feed that only changes when the reader asks.

Use role="feed" only when the app loads entries as the reader scrolls and implements the feed keyboard contract itself: each entry an article with aria-posinset and aria-setsize, and Page Down and Page Up moving between entries. The component does not provide that behaviour.

A long feed shows the latest entries. Earlier ones come in through one quiet small button, Show earlier activity, with a chevron-up icon, in gw-activity-feed__more above the first day. While they are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the button and on the section, and change the button's words to Loading earlier activity. Afterwards move focus to the first entry that was added, so the reader continues from there.
For the first fetch, an empty feed and a failed fetch, the section holds a spinner, a compact empty state or an error state in place of the days.
An excerpt is text, never markup, and is short: one command or one line of output. Longer output belongs in a tool call.
Tab reaches the Show earlier activity button and any source chips, in order. Entries themselves take no focus.

components.name: alert
components.title: Alert
components.purpose: A message inside a view about the state of what the view shows.
whenToUse: To tell the reader something about the run, task or repository on screen that changes what they should do next.
To report the result of an action where it happened, when the result should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For a mistake in one form control. Use the field's error message.
When a whole view failed to load. Use an error state.
When a view has nothing to show yet. Use an empty state.
For a confirmation that should go away by itself. Use a toast.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Context the reader may want. Label it Note.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Something finished as intended. Label it Done.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Something will go wrong unless the reader acts. Label it Warning.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Something failed. Label it Error, and say what to do about it.

accessibility: Every alert holds a gw-alert__label naming its tone in a word. The stylesheet draws the matching icon, so tone is carried by a word, an icon and a colour.
An alert that is part of the view when it loads takes no role. It is read in order with the rest of the content.
An alert the app adds in response to something takes role="status" for info, success and warning, which is announced when the screen reader is next idle.
Use role="alert" only for a failure the reader must know about now. It interrupts whatever is being read.
For the announcement to be reliable, add the element with its role first, or keep it in the page empty and hidden with the hidden attribute, then fill in the text.
The title and body are paragraphs, not headings, so an alert does not change the outline of the view.
At most one action: a gw-button gw-button--small inside gw-alert__action. Never primary. Use a link element when it goes to another view.
Do not move focus to an alert. The role announces it.

components.name: app-header
components.title: App header
components.purpose: The top bar of an app: the product name or the current view's title, with an optional back link, actions and a tray for approvals that are waiting.
whenToUse: Once per screen, as the first thing in the page.
With the product name on a top-level screen, and with a back link and the view's title on a screen below one.
With the tray when something, such as an approval, must stay in sight on every screen.
whenNotToUse: For a view's title with its description and main action inside the page. Use a page header.
For moving between the main destinations on a phone. Use a tab bar.
For a message about the state of the app, such as a lost connection. Use a banner under the header.
For the main action of a view. Put a primary button in the view, never in the header.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Scrolls away with the page. Use it when the screen is short or the header holds nothing the reader needs while scrolling.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Stays at the top while the page scrolls. Use it when the back link, the actions or the tray must stay in reach.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: One row, 52px tall, with 44px controls, at every width. The tray adds a row below it only while it holds something.

accessibility: Use a header element. Outside main it is the page's banner landmark, so a page has one.
The product name is a link to the first screen. The view title is the page's h1 when the header shows one.
The back link names where it goes: visible text such as Tasks, or aria-label="Back to tasks" when it is only the icon.
An icon-only action has an aria-label that says what it does and to what, such as Search tasks. Its icon carries aria-hidden="true".
Use a link for an action that goes to another view and a button for one that acts on this view.
Tab moves through the name or back link, then the actions, then the tray, in the order they are written. Enter follows a link, and Enter or Space presses a button.
A long title is cut with an ellipsis. Keep the full title in the document title or in the page, where it can be read whole.
An empty tray takes no space and is not announced. Leave the element in place and fill it when something is waiting.
With the sticky variant, give the scrolling container scroll-padding-top of the header's height, so a focused element is not hidden under it.

components.name: approval
components.title: Approval
components.purpose: One request from an agent that waits for the reader's answer: what would run, where, for whom and why, with Allow and Decline.
whenToUse: When an agent is blocked until the reader allows or declines a tool call or a command.
Alone in a view for one request, or as list items in a queue of several.
whenNotToUse: For a request that was already answered or denied. Use a message row in the transcript.
To say how many requests wait. Use the pending tray.
To confirm an action the reader started themselves, such as deleting a workspace. Use a dialog.

variants.name: normal
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. The risk line reads Normal risk and what keeps it so, beside an info icon.

variants.name: elevated
variants.use: A request that reaches outside the task's worktree, deletes, or cannot be undone. The risk line reads Elevated risk and why, beside a warning icon, on a tinted band.

accessibility: Use an article with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-approval__title, a heading at the level the view needs. The title says who asks and for what.

Emphasis: when a view shows a single approval, Allow may be the view's primary action, gw-button gw-button--primary. When approvals are listed, each card sits in its own li of a ul and Allow is a plain gw-button, never primary, so a queue has no competing primary actions.

Allow comes first and Decline sits at the far end of gw-approval__actions. Both are always visible, carry data-gw-critical so the checker can see they are never hidden, and are never placed inside a details element.
The risk line always starts with the words Normal risk or Elevated risk and then says why. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet, so the tone is never colour alone.
gw-approval__command holds exactly what would run, as text, with characters that cannot be seen written out. It wraps, and never scrolls sideways.
Supporting detail goes in a details element with a text summary, such as Show the full request. It holds no control the reader needs in order to answer.

A note on declining is optional. Under the actions, add a details element whose summary reads Decline with a note, holding a labelled field and its own button, Decline and send note. It starts closed, without the open attribute, and the plain Decline above it still declines with no note.

While the answer is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the pressed button, change its label to Allowing or Declining, and disable the other. If sending fails, restore both and add gw-approval__error with role="alert", saying that nothing was allowed.

Tab reaches the summary, then Allow, then Decline. Enter and Space activate each. The component needs no script: the app sets aria-busy and disabled, and removes the card once the request is answered. Move focus to the next card or the view's heading when it goes.

components.name: attachment-chip
components.title: Attachment chip
components.purpose: One file or image attached to a prompt: its kind as an icon, its name, its size in words and a button that removes it.
whenToUse: Above or below a composer, for each file or image the reader attached to the prompt they are writing.
While an attachment uploads, and when its upload fails.
whenNotToUse: For a reference to a file in the repository, a page or a commit. Use a source chip, which is a link.
For a file listed in a sent message or a changed-files list. Use a dense list.
For a status. Use a badge.
For choosing the file. Use the browser's file input, labelled as a field.

variants.name: file
variants.use: The file icon, for anything that is not an image.

variants.name: image
variants.use: The image icon, with a gw-visually-hidden span reading Image before the name, so the kind is not the icon alone.

accessibility: Each chip is an li with the class gw-attachment-chip, in a ul with an aria-label such as Attachments. Lay the ul out with gw-cluster gw-gap-md: the 12px gap keeps the remove buttons' 44px pointer targets on two rows from overlapping.

Write the whole file name as text, split into gw-attachment-chip__start and gw-attachment-chip__end with no white space between the spans. The end part is the last few characters with the extension. The stylesheet cuts the middle from view only, so a screen reader still reads the whole name.
Write the size with its unit, such as 48 KB or 2.1 MB.

The remove control is a button element with type="button" and the class gw-attachment-chip__remove, holding the x icon with aria-hidden="true" and a gw-visually-hidden span that names the file: Remove session-trace.log. It is drawn 24px square and its pointer target is 44px each way.

While the file uploads, set aria-busy="true" on the li and add a native progress element with the class gw-attachment-chip__progress as its last child, with value and max set from the upload and an aria-label such as Uploading session-trace.log. Leave value off until the first figure arrives. Put the percentage and the size in gw-attachment-chip__size, and name the button Cancel the upload of and the file.

When the upload fails, remove aria-busy and the progress element and add a p with the class gw-attachment-chip__error and role="alert" as the last child. It says what happened and what to do, such as Not attached: files can be up to 10 MB. Remove it and attach a smaller file. Its icon and the chip's outline are drawn by the stylesheet.
While the prompt is being sent, set the disabled attribute on each remove button.
After a chip is removed, move focus to the next chip's remove button, or to the composer when none is left.
Tab reaches each remove button. Enter and Space activate it. The component needs no script of its own: the app sets aria-busy, the progress value, the text and the disabled attribute.

components.name: avatar
components.title: Avatar
components.purpose: A small square mark for a person or an agent, holding initials, an icon or an image, with the name beside it.
whenToUse: To say who did something or who something belongs to: the author of a message, the actor of an event, the owner of a task.
With an icon for an agent and initials or an image for a person, so the two are told apart by shape as well as by name.
With the small size in a dense row, a timeline entry or a line of text.
whenNotToUse: As decoration, or in a stack of overlapping marks. Write the names, or a count such as 4 reviewers.
Without a name, unless the name is already written directly beside it. Then give the mark an accessible name.
For a repository, a branch or a file. Use text, with an icon in a list row where it helps.
For a status. Use a badge. The mark carries no tone and no status dot.

variants.name: initials
variants.use: The default. One or two capital letters in a span with the class gw-avatar__mark.

variants.name: icon
variants.use: An svg with the class gw-avatar__icon inside the mark, for an agent or a system actor.

variants.name: image
variants.use: An img with the class gw-avatar__mark in place of the span. It needs an alt attribute, width and height. The picture is cropped to the square.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: A 32px mark with the name in medium weight.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: A 24px mark with the name at normal weight, for dense rows and lines of text.

accessibility: Use a span with the class gw-avatar holding the mark and then the name in a span with the class gw-avatar__name. The name is visible by default and is what a screen reader reads.
Beside a visible name the mark is decoration: give a span mark aria-hidden="true", and an image mark alt="". The alt attribute is always present on an img.
With no visible name, the mark must carry the name: role="img" and aria-label on a span mark, or the name as the alt text of an image mark.
Say what kind of actor it is in words when it matters, such as Claude Code, implementer. The icon alone does not say it.
If an image fails to load, replace the img with the initials span. The stylesheet cannot do this.
An avatar is not focusable and takes no press. To link to a profile, put the whole avatar inside a link.

components.name: banner
components.title: Banner
components.purpose: One message about the state of the whole app, across the full width under the app header.
whenToUse: For a condition that affects every screen and is still true, such as a lost connection, a paused agent host or a session about to end.
Directly under the app header, across the full width, for as long as the condition lasts.
With one action when there is one thing the reader can do about it, such as Retry.
whenNotToUse: For the result of something the reader just did, such as Task saved. Confirm it where it happened, or use a toast.
For a problem with one field or one form. Use the field's error message.
For a problem with one item in a view, such as a failed run. Show it on that item.
For a decision the reader must make before going on. Use a dialog.
For more than one message at a time. Show the most severe one.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Something the reader should know that needs no action, such as a planned restart or a restored connection. Set role="status".

variants.name: warning

variants.name: danger

accessibility: Set role="status" on an info or warning banner, so a screen reader announces it when the reader pauses. Set role="alert" on a danger banner, so it is announced at once.

Do not set aria-busy on the banner. A screen reader holds back the announcement of a busy region. While the action runs, set aria-busy="true" on the action button and change its label, such as Retrying.
The stylesheet draws the tone's icon, so the tone never depends on colour and needs no markup. The text carries the whole message.

The action and the dismiss button sit together in a gw-banner__actions element after the text. The action is one gw-button gw-button--small, with a label that says what it does. Do not make it primary.
The dismiss button is a button with aria-label="Dismiss", and its icon carries aria-hidden="true". Offer it only when the message is safe to lose. When it is pressed, move focus to the main content.
Tab reaches the action and then the dismiss button, in that order. Enter and Space press them.
The banner does not take focus when it appears, so it never interrupts typing.

components.name: composer
components.title: Composer
components.purpose: The prompt input under a transcript: a textarea that grows with its content, and Send.
whenToUse: At the bottom of a transcript, to send the next prompt to the agent.
To stop a running turn from the same place the reader sends from.
whenNotToUse: For one line of text in a form, such as a task title. Use a field.
For longer text that is saved with a form and not sent as a message. Use a textarea.
To answer an approval request. Use the approval's own Allow and Decline.

variants.name: default
variants.use: In the flow of the page, as wide as its container.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: Held to the bottom of the scrolling view, with a top border, its own padding and room for the home indicator. Make the view's scroller end at the visible viewport, with a height in dvh or interactive-widget=resizes-content in the viewport meta tag, so it stays above an on-screen keyboard.

Send is a button of type submit with gw-button gw-button--primary. It is the view's one primary action, so nothing else in the view is primary.

When the reader cannot send, set disabled on the textarea and on Send, and say why in gw-composer__reason, linked from both by aria-describedby. The reason says what to do next.
When a prompt fails to send, keep the text in the textarea and add gw-composer__error with role="alert", linked by aria-describedby. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Tab moves from the textarea to Send, then to the quiet controls. The app decides whether Enter sends. If it does, Shift+Enter adds a line, and the button remains the way to send on a phone.

components.name: confirm-dialog
components.title: Confirm dialog
components.purpose: A dialog that asks before something is deleted or discarded, and says in plain words what will be lost.
whenToUse: Before an action the reader started that deletes or discards something and cannot be undone, such as deleting a workspace or discarding a draft.
whenNotToUse: For an action that can be reversed. Do it at once and show an undo toast.
For a request from an agent that waits for an answer. Use an approval.
For a task with fields to fill in. Use a dialog.
To confirm an ordinary action such as saving. Do not ask.
accessibility: Use the dialog markup with both classes on the dialog element, gw-dialog and gw-confirm-dialog, and add role="alertdialog". A screen reader then reads the question and its description at once, where a plain dialog would read only the title.
Point aria-labelledby at the title and aria-describedby at gw-dialog__body, so the list of what is lost is part of what is read.

The title names the thing: Delete the workspace api-refactor? The body says what will be lost, one thing per gw-confirm-dialog__loss, and that it cannot be undone. Say what is kept when the reader might fear for it.

Cancel is the first button and the destructive button the second. Open with showModal(), which moves focus to the first button, so focus starts on Cancel. Never put autofocus on the destructive button.
The destructive button is gw-button gw-button--danger and repeats the verb and the thing: Delete workspace. It is never gw-button--primary, and a confirm dialog has no primary button.
The footer carries gw-dialog__footer and gw-confirm-dialog__actions, which holds Cancel at the start and the destructive button at the far end.
Escape cancels. Both buttons close the dialog through the form with method="dialog", and the app deletes only when dialog.returnValue is the destructive button's value.

While deleting, set aria-busy="true" on the destructive button, change its label and disable Cancel. If it fails, keep the dialog open and put an alert with role="alert" at the top of the body saying that nothing was deleted and what to do.

components.purpose: A read-only value the reader takes somewhere else, with a button that copies it.
whenToUse: For a value the reader will paste into a terminal or another tool: a branch name, a commit hash, a path, a command.
When the value is one line. A long one is cut short with an ellipsis and still copies whole.
whenNotToUse: For a value the reader can change. Use a text input in a field.
For several lines, such as a log or a diff. Show them in a pre element.
For a value nobody needs to copy. Write it as plain text.
For a secret that must stay hidden. This component always shows its value.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as its container, with the button at its natural width. Limit the width on the container.

accessibility: The value is an input element with type="text" and the readonly attribute, never disabled. It stays in the tab order, its text can be selected, and the arrow keys scroll a long value.
Name the input with a label element, usually by putting the copy field inside gw-field after its gw-field__label, or with aria-label when the view has no room for a visible label.
The button is a gw-button with the visible label Copy. Give it an aria-label that names the value, such as Copy branch name, so several on one view can be told apart.
Keep an empty gw-copy-field__status element with role="status" in the page from the start. role="status" is a polite live region, the same as aria-live="polite".
After a copy, the app sets the status text to say what was copied, such as Branch name copied. A screen reader announces it and sighted readers see the same words. Clear the text after a few seconds.
If the copy fails, the app sets the status text to say so and what to do: select the value and copy it by hand.

components.name: data-table
components.title: Data table
components.purpose: Things compared across columns on a real table: a caption, sortable headers, numeric columns, one action for each row, rows that expand, and a stacked layout on a phone.
whenToUse: When the reader compares the same facts across several things: runs by duration and tokens, repositories by usage, branches by age.
With the default stacked layout when each row can be read by itself on a phone: below 768px a row becomes a block and each cell prints its column label beside its value.
With the scroll variant when the reader compares down a column even on a phone, or when the headers sort: the columns stay and the table scrolls sideways inside its wrapper.
With the sticky variant for a table long enough that the header would scroll out of sight.
whenNotToUse: For things the reader scans and opens, with one or two facts each. Use the list.
For the facts of one thing. Use the key-value list.
For layout. A table is for data with column headers.
For a sortable table in the stacked layout. The header row is not drawn below 768px, so its buttons would be out of reach: use the scroll variant, or offer the order in a select above the table.
For a row with two or more actions. Open the row's own view, or put the rest in its detail row.
For a table nested in a table's detail row. Put facts there as text or a key-value list.

variants.name: stacked
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. Columns at 768px and wider. Below that each row is a block: its th is the block's title and each td prints the label in its data-label attribute beside its value. The header row is not drawn.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: Columns at every width. Put the table inside a div with the class gw-data-table__scroll, which scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit. Cells do not wrap.

variants.name: sticky
variants.use: The header row stays at the top of whatever scrolls the table up and down, on the page surface. It has no effect inside gw-data-table__scroll unless the app gives that wrapper a height, and none in the stacked layout below 768px.

accessibility: Use a table with a caption, gw-data-table__caption, that says what the rows are. Column headers are th scope="col" in a thead, and the cell that names each row is a th scope="row". Do not build a table from divs.

Give every td a data-label attribute holding the text of its column header. Below 768px the stylesheet prints it beside the value, and it is read out with the value. Leave it off the action cell, a detail cell and a state cell.
A cell holds one run of text or one element. In the stacked layout a second element would start a new line under the label.
A column of numbers carries gw-data-table__numeric on its th and on every td: right-aligned, in tabular figures, each number with its unit.

A sortable header is a button with the class gw-data-table__sort inside the th, holding the header's words. Set aria-sort="ascending" or aria-sort="descending" on the th of the one column the rows are ordered by, and leave it off the others. The stylesheet draws the direction from that attribute. The app reorders the rows and moves the attribute, and the caption or a role="status" line says the new order.

A row has at most one action: a small quiet button in a td with the class gw-data-table__action, the last cell of the row, under a th whose text is in a gw-visually-hidden span. When every row's button has the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the row. The cell pads the 32px button out to 44px, so its pointer target fits the row and a one-line row is no taller.

A row that expands has a button with the class gw-data-table__expand in its th, holding the words that name the row, with aria-expanded and with aria-controls pointing at the next row. That next row is a tr with the class gw-data-table__detail holding one td that spans every column. The app sets aria-expanded to true or false and nothing else: the stylesheet does not draw the detail row while the button says false. Do not use the hidden attribute on the detail row.
Mark the selected row with aria-selected="true" on its tr. It is drawn with a bar at its start as well as a shade.

With no rows, while loading and after a failure, keep the caption and the header and put one row in the tbody whose single td has the class gw-data-table__state and spans every column. Empty: a gw-data-table__message sentence saying why, and at most one small button. Loading: a spinner with role="status", and aria-busy="true" on the table. Error: a gw-data-table__message with role="alert" that says what to do, and a small Retry button. The stylesheet draws the failure's icon.
A status in a cell is written in words. One badge may hold it.

The wrapper of the scroll variant carries tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-labelledby pointing at the caption's id, so a keyboard can scroll it with the arrow keys. Give each such table on a view a different caption.
Tab moves through the header buttons, then each row's expand button and action, in order. Enter and Space activate them. There are no arrow-key bindings between cells.

The numbers are right-aligned in tabular figures with their units, and on a phone each row becomes a block whose cells print their column label from data-label.

components.name: dialog
components.title: Dialog
components.purpose: A modal window for one short task that must be finished or cancelled before the reader goes on.
whenToUse: For a short task the reader starts from the current view and finishes in one step, such as renaming a branch.
To ask a question the view cannot go on without, with one primary action and Cancel.
whenNotToUse: To confirm deleting or discarding something. Use the confirm dialog.
For a longer form, filters or the details of an item. Use a sheet.
For supplementary content beside a control that should not block the page. Use a popover.
To report that something happened. Use a toast, or an alert for a result that stays.

variants.name: default
variants.use: No modifier class. The dialog grows with its content and scrolls as a whole once it reaches the height of the screen.

variants.name: scroll
variants.use: A body that may be long, such as a list of files. The title and the footer stay in place and the body scrolls between two rules.

accessibility: Use a dialog element with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-dialog__title, an h2. When the body is one short text, point aria-describedby at it.

Open it with the one line document.getElementById("dialog-id").showModal(). That call traps focus, makes the page behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener when the dialog closes. Do not write the open attribute yourself, which shows the dialog without any of that: the examples carry it only so they are drawn in the gallery.

As progressive enhancement, the opener may carry command="show-modal" and commandfor="dialog-id", and then needs no script where invoker commands are supported. Keep the showModal() call for browsers without them.

Wrap the content in a form with method="dialog" and the class gw-dialog__panel. Each footer button is a submit button with a value. Pressing one closes the dialog with no script, and the app reads dialog.returnValue in a close event listener. To validate or save before closing, handle the form's submit event and call preventDefault().
The primary button comes first in the footer and Cancel second, so Enter in a field takes the primary action. Cancel carries formnovalidate so it closes a form with an empty required field.
showModal() moves focus to the first focusable element, or to the one that has the autofocus attribute. Tab stays inside the dialog.
A dialog has one primary button. It is a view of its own, so the page behind may have its own.
With gw-dialog--scroll, if the body holds no control, give gw-dialog__body tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label so the keyboard can scroll it.

While saving, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button, change its label to say what is happening and disable Cancel. If it fails, keep the dialog open and say what happened and what to do, in the field's error or in an alert inside the body.

components.name: diff
components.title: Diff
components.purpose: One file's change as a unified diff, with its path and how many lines were added and removed.
whenToUse: To show what a task changed in one file, before the reader decides on it.
One diff per file. For several files, list them and put each diff in a row disclosure.
The counts alone, gw-diff__counts, beside a file's name in a list row or a disclosure summary.
whenNotToUse: For a file's contents with no change, or for a command's output. Use the code block.
For two versions side by side. This component is unified only, which is what fits a phone.
For a change to prose that the reader edits in place. Show the text itself.
accessibility: Use a figure. Its figcaption, gw-diff__header, holds the path in a code element and the counts. Leave the header out when the diff sits under a summary that already shows both.
Write each count as a sign and a number followed by a gw-diff__label span that finishes it in words, such as +7 and lines added. The label is hidden from sight and read by a screen reader.

Each line is a gw-diff__line holding a gw-diff__sign cell and a gw-diff__text cell. Use an ins element for an added line and a del element for a removed one, with the plus or minus as the sign. A context line and a hunk header are spans, with a space as the sign.
Never leave out the sign. The shading alone does not mark a line for someone who cannot tell the colours apart.

While the diff is fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the figure and put a gw-diff__note with role="status" in place of the body. When it fails, use a note with role="alert" that says why. The stylesheet adds the failure's icon.

components.name: disclosure
components.title: Disclosure
components.purpose: A native details element that shows or hides detail under a summary written in text.
whenToUse: For detail most readers can do without: a log, the environment, the steps of a finished attempt.
With the row variant inside a list row, for a changed file that opens to its diff. The summary holds the path and the counts.
For the one group of advanced settings in a view. Mark that details element with data-gw-advanced.
whenNotToUse: For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical that can be reached only inside closed content fails the hidden-critical-action rule: show it in the view too, or open the disclosure by default.
Nested more than two levels. A third level fails the disclosure-depth rule: move that content to a view of its own.
With a summary that is only an icon or is empty. A summary without text fails the summary-without-text rule.
For a list of actions that opens over the page. Use a menu.
For sections where opening one must close the others. This component has no script, so each disclosure opens and closes alone.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Stands alone. Its content is indented to start under the summary's text.

variants.name: row
variants.use: The only child of a gw-list__row. The summary is the row, and the content uses the row's full width, which a diff needs at phone width.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The summary is at least 44px tall and as wide as the disclosure. It grows when its text wraps.

accessibility: Use a details element with a summary as its first child. The browser gives the summary its role and its expanded state, and the open attribute is the only state: never toggle a class.
The summary holds text that says what is inside. The chevron is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup. Do not put a heading, a button or a link inside the summary.

Trailing text such as a count goes in a gw-disclosure__meta span inside the summary, after the label. It is read as part of the summary's name, so write counts in words or with a hidden label, as gw-diff__counts does.
Put the content in one gw-disclosure__content element after the summary.

Tab reaches the summary. Enter and Space open and close it. Both come from the summary element. Closed content is out of the tab order and is skipped by a screen reader, and the browser's find-in-page opens it.
Set the open attribute in markup to start open. Start open when the content holds an action the reader needs.
Fetch heavy content, such as a diff, when the disclosure opens, and show the content's own loading state until it arrives.

components.purpose: What a view shows when it has no data yet, with the way to get some.
whenToUse: In place of a list, table or panel that has nothing in it yet.

whenNotToUse: While the data is still loading. Use a spinner.

components.name: error-state
components.title: Error state
components.purpose: What a view shows when its data could not be loaded, with a way to try again.
whenToUse: In place of a list, table, panel or whole view whose data failed to load.
When the reader can do something about it, at least trying again.
whenNotToUse: When the view loaded and one action in it failed. Use an alert beside that action.
For a mistake in a form control. Use the field's error message.
When the view loaded and has nothing in it. Use an empty state.
accessibility: Set role="alert" on the error state when it replaces content after a failed load, so a screen reader announces it. Leave the role off while a retry is running, so the same failure is not announced twice.

components.name: feedback
components.title: Feedback
components.purpose: A control for rating an agent's answer as helpful or not helpful, with an optional follow-up note and a confirmation.
whenToUse: Under an agent's answer or at the end of a turn, to record whether it helped.
When a rating can be followed by an optional note on what was wrong.
whenNotToUse: To answer a request an agent is waiting on. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
To accept or reject a run's work. Use buttons that name the action, such as Accept changes.
For a rating on a scale, or a choice among several options. Use radio inputs in a field.
For a setting that turns something on or off. Use a checkbox or a switch.
accessibility: Use a div with role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at gw-feedback__prompt, which asks the question in words, such as Was this answer helpful?

Each choice is a button element with type="button" and the classes gw-button gw-button--small gw-feedback__choice, and the two sit together in gw-feedback__choices. It holds an icon with aria-hidden="true" and the words Helpful or Not helpful. Never use the icon alone.

Both buttons carry aria-pressed. The app sets aria-pressed="true" on the chosen one and "false" on the other. Pressing the chosen button again clears the rating. The pressed button is drawn with a darker outline, a shade and a heavier label, not a colour alone.

Keep an empty p with the class gw-feedback__confirmation and role="status" in the group from the start. After a choice is saved, the app writes one line into it, such as Rated helpful. Thank you., and a screen reader announces it. It takes no room while empty.

The follow-up note is an app-set pattern, not a state of the component. After a choice, the app inserts gw-feedback__note between the row and the confirmation, or removes its hidden attribute: a gw-field whose control is a gw-textarea, with a visible label, and a secondary button, Send note. The rating is saved by the first press, and the note is optional. Do not move focus into the field: the reader reaches it with Tab.
After the note is sent, set the disabled attribute on both choices, leave aria-pressed as it is, remove the note field and say so in the confirmation.

If saving fails, set both buttons back to aria-pressed="false" and add a p with the class gw-feedback__error and role="alert" that says the rating was not saved and what to do. Its icon is drawn by the stylesheet.
Tab reaches Helpful, then Not helpful, then the note field and Send note when shown. Enter and Space press a button. The buttons are drawn 32px tall with a 44px pointer target.

components.name: inspector
components.title: Inspector
components.purpose: A panel for the details of the item selected in the content beside it, with a title, a close button and sections of labelled values.
whenToUse: When the reader picks an item in a list, a board or a diff and wants its facts while the list stays in view: the branch, timing and usage of a run.
At 768px and up, as the second child of gw-inspector__layout, where it is a column after the content.

Below 768px, either stacked under the content in the same layout, or opened over it as a sheet. The sheet is the app's dialog pattern, a dialog element holding the same aside markup, opened when a row is pressed and closed by the same close button. This component does not style the sheet.
whenNotToUse: For the destinations of the app. Use the sidebar nav.
For an item the reader will work in for a while, such as a transcript. Give it a screen of its own.
For a request that waits for an answer. Use an approval.
For a form with several steps. The panel shows facts and at most a few actions.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 288px wide beside the content at 768px and up, with a rule on its leading edge. Full width under the content below that, with a rule above it.

accessibility: Use an aside with the gw-inspector class and an aria-label that names the item, such as Details of run 4182. Change the label when the selection changes.
gw-inspector__header holds the title, a heading with the gw-inspector__title class at the level the view needs, and the close button.

The close button is a button with the classes gw-button, gw-button--quiet and gw-inspector__close. It holds the x icon with aria-hidden="true" and its name in a gw-visually-hidden span, such as Close details of run 4182. When it is pressed the app removes the aside, or sets the hidden attribute on it, clears the selection and moves focus back to the row that was selected.

Each gw-inspector__section has a heading with the gw-inspector__heading class and a dl with the gw-inspector__facts class. Each fact is a div with the gw-inspector__fact class holding a dt, gw-inspector__label, and a dd, gw-inspector__value. A value is written in words with its unit.
Mark the selected item in the content with aria-current="true", as a list row does, so the reader can tell what the panel describes without relying on position.
Selecting an item does not move focus into the panel. The panel follows the content in the markup, so Tab reaches it after the list.

With nothing selected, either leave the aside out or show one gw-inspector__note sentence that says what to select. While the details are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the aside and show a spinner with text. When the fetch fails, show an alert that says what to do.
The component needs no script of its own. The app fills the panel, sets aria-label and handles the close button.

whenToUse: For the facts of one run, task, repository or request: its branch, its path, when it started, what it cost.
Inside a card or a disclosure, or straight on the page under a heading.
With mono values for anything the reader may copy or compare character by character: a path, a commit hash, a command, a branch name.
whenNotToUse: For the same facts about several things. Use the data table, where each thing is a row.

components.name: menu
components.title: Menu
components.purpose: A list of actions on one thing, opened from a button.
whenToUse: For three or more actions on one item that do not all fit beside it, such as the actions on a task or a run.
For the less common actions of a view, behind a button that names what they act on.
whenNotToUse: For one or two actions. Show them as buttons.
For the main action of a view. Show it as the primary button.
To choose a value in a form. Use a select.
To move between views. Use links, a tab bar or a sidebar.
For content that is not a list of actions. Use a popover.

variants.name: item
variants.use: The default item, with no modifier class. An optional gw-menu__icon comes before its text.

variants.name: danger item
variants.use: An item that deletes or cannot be undone. It is last, below a gw-menu__divider, and its label names what is lost.

accessibility: Give the menu the popover attribute, an id, role="menu" and an aria-label. Give the button popovertarget with that id and aria-haspopup="menu". The browser opens and closes the menu, sets aria-expanded on the button, closes on Escape and on a press outside, and returns focus to the button.

Put the menu straight after its button in the markup. Each item is a button with type="button", role="menuitem" and the class gw-menu__item. Its label is a verb and what it acts on. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
A section is a div with role="group", the class gw-menu__section and aria-labelledby pointing at its gw-menu__label, which carries role="presentation". A divider is an hr with gw-menu__divider.

An unavailable item carries aria-disabled="true", so it stays in the arrow-key order and a screen reader can find it, and the app ignores presses on it. Say why in its label when the reason is not obvious.

Without script the menu still works: Tab moves through the items and Enter or Space activates one. The arrow keys are the one thing the app, or the system's behaviours module, adds, as a roving focus: when the menu opens (its toggle event), move focus to the first item. Give every item tabindex="-1" except the one that has focus. Down and Up move focus to the next and the previous item and wrap at the ends, Home and End go to the first and the last, and a letter key goes to the next item that starts with it. Tab closes the menu.
After an item's action runs, the app closes the menu with hidePopover(), and focus returns to the button.

components.title: Pagination
components.purpose: Previous and next for a list split into pages, with the position written in words and optional numbered pages.
whenToUse: Under a list or table that is split into pages the reader may want to return to by number or by address, such as finished runs.
With numbered pages when the reader jumps around, such as to the last page. They show at 768px and up only.
whenNotToUse: For a list of one page. Show no pagination at all.
To reveal the rest of a short list in place. Use show more, with its Show all button.

For the steps of a form. Use buttons named for each step.

variants.use: The default: the status and the two buttons. The whole component at phone width.

accessibility: Use a nav element with an aria-label that says what is paged, such as Pages of runs. It holds the status and then gw-pagination__controls.
The status is a p with the gw-pagination__status class that reads Page 3 of 12. The app writes both numbers. It comes first in the markup and is drawn between the buttons at phone width.

Previous and Next are links with the gw-button class, plus gw-pagination__previous or gw-pagination__next, and rel="prev" or rel="next". Each has its word as text, then page in a gw-visually-hidden span, so its name is Previous page or Next page. The chevron is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".

On the first page Previous has no href, and takes role="link" and aria-disabled="true". On the last page Next does. It stays in place so the buttons do not move, is announced as unavailable, and is not a tab stop.

When the app pages in place with script instead of addresses, use button elements with the same classes and the disabled attribute at the ends, then move focus to the heading of the list after each change.

A numbered page is a link with the gw-pagination__page class inside an li, holding Page in a gw-visually-hidden span and then the number. Set aria-current="page" on the current one, which draws its border and heavier number. A gap is an li with the gw-pagination__gap class and aria-hidden="true".

whenToUse: For work that can be counted: 7 of 12 checks passed, 96 of 213 tests run, 31 of 48 files uploaded.

variants.name: indeterminate

accessibility: Markup, in this order: a label with the gw-progress__label class and a for attribute, a p with the gw-progress__value class, and a progress element with the gw-progress__bar class and the id the label names. The stylesheet draws the bar under the two lines of text.

accessibility: It is the content of a list row: a span with the class gw-run-status inside the gw-list__link or gw-list__content of an li with the class gw-list__row, in a ul with the class gw-list. Every part is a span, so it is valid inside a link.

The parts come in reading order: gw-run-status__title, gw-run-status__station, gw-run-status__facts. A screen reader reads the row as its title, its station, then who is acting and for how long. Below 768px the station sits under the title, and from 768px the row is one line with the station at its end.

gw-run-status__station holds one badge with the station in words: Queued, Building, Verifying, Reviewing, Awaiting decision, Blocked, Interrupted or Decided. Use the same word, tone and icon for a station everywhere. The badge icon carries aria-hidden="true".

gw-run-status__facts says who or what is acting in words, such as Claude Code, implementer or Waiting on you, then the elapsed time in a time element with the class gw-run-status__elapsed and a datetime duration. Write the time with its unit: 4 min 12 s. A time that ticks is not in a live region.

A row has at most one action, and only when the run waits on the reader: a gw-button gw-button--small in the row's gw-list__action, after the link, never primary. Its aria-label starts with its visible words and names the run, such as Resume Fix the login timeout.
When a station changes while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the row.
Tab reaches the row's link and then its action. Enter follows the link. The component needs no script.

components.name: search-field
components.title: Search field
components.purpose: A search input with a search icon, an optional clear button and a line that counts the results.
whenToUse: To search or filter a list the reader can see, such as runs, branches or changed files.
At the top of the list it filters, with the count line between the field and the results.
whenNotToUse: For any other text value, such as a branch name to create. Use a field.
To pick one of a known, short set. Use a select or a segmented control.
As the only way to reach an item. The list stays browsable without a search.

variants.name: visible label
variants.use: The default. A label with gw-search-field__label above the input.

variants.name: hidden label
variants.use: The same label with gw-visually-hidden added, where the list's heading already says what is searched. The label element stays in the markup.

variants.name: with a clear button
variants.use: A button with gw-search-field__clear after the input. Leave it out where the field is cleared some other way.

accessibility: Use input type="search" carrying gw-field__control and gw-search-field__input, inside a div with gw-search-field__box. The search icon is drawn by the stylesheet and needs no markup.
Every search field has a label element with gw-search-field__label tied to the input by for and id. Add gw-visually-hidden to hide it from sight. A placeholder is a hint, never the label.

The outer element with gw-search-field is a form with role="search" and an aria-label when it is the search for the page, and a plain div when it filters one list in place. Give each search landmark on a page a different label.

The clear button is a button with gw-search-field__clear, placed after the input, holding its name in a span with gw-visually-hidden, such as Clear the search. Its cross is drawn by the stylesheet and its target is 44px square.

With type="reset" inside a form the clear button needs no script, as long as the form is served with an empty value. Otherwise use type="button", and the app empties the input and moves focus back to it.
The clear button is hidden while the input is empty. That relies on the input having a placeholder attribute: give it hint text, or a single space where no hint is wanted.

The count line is a p with gw-search-field__count and aria-live="polite". Keep it in the page from the start, and change only its text when the results change, after the reader pauses typing, so a screen reader announces the new count without losing focus. It gives a number and its unit, such as 3 of 128 runs match "session".
While results load, the count line says what is being searched. With no results it says so, repeats the query and says what to try next. The stylesheet has no styling of its own for either.
When the input is disabled, say why in the count line and link it with aria-describedby. Leave aria-live off a line that never changes.
Tab reaches the input and then the clear button. Escape clears the input in browsers that support it for a search input, and Enter submits the form.

components.name: segmented-control
components.title: Segmented control
components.purpose: Two to five short options of which exactly one is chosen, shown side by side.
whenToUse: To switch how the same content is shown, such as a unified or a split diff.
To filter a list by one of a few values, such as the status of a run.
When every option has a label of one or two words and all of them should stay visible.
whenNotToUse: For more than five options, or labels longer than two words. Use a select or a radio group.
To move between views or pages. Use links, or the tab bar for an app's main destinations.
For a single on-or-off setting. Use a switch.
For actions, such as Rerun failed and Rerun all. Use an attached button group.
accessibility: Use a fieldset with gw-segmented-control and a legend with gw-segmented-control__legend that names the choice. Add gw-visually-hidden to the legend where a heading beside the control already names it. The legend stays in the markup.

Inside a div with gw-segmented-control__options, each option is a label with gw-segmented-control__option holding input type="radio" with gw-segmented-control__input and then a span with gw-segmented-control__label. The label element names the radio, and the span must come straight after the input.
Every input has the same name attribute, different from every other group on the page, and one input has the checked attribute from the start.
It needs no script: the browser keeps exactly one option chosen. An app that reacts at once listens for the change event on the fieldset.
The chosen option is a raised segment with a border and heavier text, so it does not rest on colour.
Disable one option with the disabled attribute on its input, or the whole control with disabled on the fieldset.
Tab moves into the control, to the chosen option. The arrow keys move between options and choose as they go. All of it comes from the native radios.

Each segment is at least 44px wide and its pointer target is 44px tall. The segments share the row equally at every width, and a label too long for its segment wraps inside it, so the control never scrolls sideways.

components.name: select
components.title: Select
components.purpose: A native select as the control of a field, for one choice from a short fixed list.
whenToUse: For one choice from a list the app already knows: a base branch, a repository, a model.
When the list is too long to show as radio buttons, from about five options up.
whenNotToUse: For two to four options the reader should compare. Use a radio group.
For on or off. Use a checkbox.
For a list long enough to need searching, or for free text. Use a text input in a field.
For a menu of actions. Use buttons.

sizes.use: 44px tall and as wide as the field. Limit the width on the field's container.

accessibility: Use a select element carrying both gw-field__control and gw-select__control, wrapped in an element with gw-select, inside gw-field. The wrapper only draws the chevron.

The keyboard is the browser's own: Space or Enter opens the list, the arrow keys move, typing jumps to a matching option, Escape closes.
The chevron is decoration drawn by the stylesheet. It needs no markup and takes no pointer events.

components.name: sheet
components.title: Sheet
components.purpose: A panel for a longer form or the details of an item, rising from the bottom edge on a phone and sitting as a side panel at 768px and wider.
whenToUse: For a form too long for a dialog, such as a new task or a set of filters.
To show the details of one item without leaving the list it came from.
whenNotToUse: For one question or one field. Use a dialog.
To confirm deleting something. Use the confirm dialog.
For a few lines of supplementary content beside a control. Use a popover.
For a list of actions. Use a menu.
For content the reader should be able to link to or come back to. Give it a view of its own.
accessibility: Use a dialog element with the class gw-sheet and aria-labelledby pointing at gw-sheet__title, an h2.

Open it with the one line document.getElementById("sheet-id").showModal(). That call traps focus, makes the page behind inert, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener. As progressive enhancement the opener may carry command="show-modal" and commandfor="sheet-id". Do not write the open attribute yourself: the examples carry it only so they are drawn in the gallery.

gw-sheet__header is a form with method="dialog" holding the title and the Close button, so Close works with no script. Close is a quiet button with only an icon, and its aria-label says what it closes.
The body is gw-sheet__body and scrolls. The footer is gw-sheet__footer, outside the body, and holds the sheet's one primary button first. Never put the primary action in the body.

When the footer's button submits fields in the body, wrap the body and the footer in a second form with the class gw-sheet__form. With method="dialog" its buttons close the sheet and the app reads dialog.returnValue in a close event listener. To validate or save first, handle the submit event and call preventDefault().
A body with no control in it that may scroll takes tabindex="0", role="group" and an aria-label, so the keyboard can scroll it.

The sheet slides in when showModal() opens it and the reset removes the movement for readers who ask for reduced motion. It keeps clear of the home indicator with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), which needs viewport-fit=cover in the page's viewport meta tag to be more than zero.

While the body loads, show a spinner with its text in the body. If loading fails, show an alert there that says what to do. While the form is sent, set aria-busy="true" on the primary button and disable the other footer buttons.

components.name: show-more
components.title: Show more
components.purpose: A control after the first part of long content that reveals the rest: a details element for text, code or a log, and a quiet button for a list cut short.
whenToUse: For a log, an output or a description that is long, when its first lines are enough for most readers and the rest is already in the page.
With the Show all button, under a list that shows its first rows, when the full list is short enough to read in one view, about fifty rows at most.
whenNotToUse: For detail under a title of its own, such as Environment. Use a disclosure, whose summary names what it holds.
For a list of hundreds of rows. Use pagination.
For anything the reader must see or do in order to go on. An action marked data-gw-critical in the hidden part fails the hidden-critical-action rule.
For content that fits in a few lines. Show all of it.

variants.name: details
variants.use: gw-show-more__rest is a details element after the part that is always shown. Its summary, gw-show-more__toggle, holds two spans: gw-show-more__more, such as Show 38 more lines, and gw-show-more__less, Show less. The stylesheet shows the one that applies. Needs no script.

variants.name: list
variants.use: A button with the classes gw-button, gw-button--quiet and gw-show-more__all after a gw-list, reading Show all 24 tasks. The app adds the rows when it is pressed.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: The control is 44px tall, as wide as its text, and starts at the content's leading edge.

accessibility: Wrap the part that is always shown and the control in a div with the gw-show-more class. The shown part comes first.

Details variant: the app writes the count into gw-show-more__more when it renders, as the number of hidden units and the unit in words: Show 38 more lines, Show 2 more paragraphs. The count is the total minus what is shown. gw-show-more__less always reads Show less.

Only one of the two spans is rendered at a time, so the summary's name is Show 38 more lines while closed and Show less while open, and the browser announces collapsed or expanded with it. The summary always holds text.
Once open, the control is drawn under the revealed content, and stays before it in the markup. Focus stays on the control, and the next Tab or reading step goes into the revealed content.

List variant: the button's label gives the full count and the noun, Show all 24 tasks. When it is pressed the app appends the remaining rows to the same list, removes the button, and moves focus to the first new row. There is no Show less.

While the rows are fetched, set aria-busy="true" on the button and change its label to Loading 21 more tasks. If the fetch fails, restore the label and add a p with the gw-show-more__error class and role="alert" before the button, saying what to do.
Tab reaches the control. Enter and Space activate it. Both come from the summary or the button element.
The browser's find-in-page opens a closed details that holds a match.

components.name: sidebar-nav
components.title: Sidebar nav
components.purpose: The destinations of an app in a column beside the content at 768px and up, each with an icon and a text label, grouped into labelled sections.
whenToUse: For moving between the screens of an app at 768px and wider, as the first child of gw-sidebar-layout.

Together with the tab bar: the sidebar is not shown below 768px, where the tab bar lists the two to five main destinations along the bottom. Put both in the markup, with the same destinations in the same order.
When there are more destinations than a tab bar holds. The sidebar lists them all, in sections, and the tab bar keeps the five most used.
whenNotToUse: Below 768px. It is not shown there, so use the tab bar for the main destinations.
For switching between panels inside one view. Use tabs.
For the details of a selected item beside the content. Use the inspector.
For an action such as New task. A destination is a screen, so use a button in the view.
For a screen that does not exist yet. List only screens that exist.

variants.name: with sections
variants.use: Each gw-sidebar-nav__section holds a gw-sidebar-nav__heading and a gw-sidebar-nav__items list. Use it for six destinations or more.

variants.name: flat
variants.use: One gw-sidebar-nav__items list directly in the nav, with no section and no heading. Use it for five destinations or fewer.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 220px wide, with each item 44px tall. Shown only at 768px and up.

accessibility: Use a nav element with an aria-label, such as Main. When the tab bar is also in the markup it may carry the same label, because only one of the two is ever shown and the other is out of the accessibility tree.

Each list of items is a ul of li, each holding one link with the gw-sidebar-nav__item class. A section's heading is a p with an id, and the section's ul points at it with aria-labelledby, so the list is announced by its section name.

Set aria-current="page" on the link for the screen that is open, and on no other. It draws the bar, the shade and the heavier label, and is what a screen reader announces. Never mark the current item with a class.

Every item has a text label in gw-sidebar-nav__label. The icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". A label too long for the column is cut with an ellipsis, so keep labels to one to three words.
Tab moves through the items in order and Enter follows one. Both come from the link element.
Keep the items in the same order on every screen.
gw-sidebar-nav__footer is optional and comes last. It holds a gw-sidebar-nav__items list or a gw-sidebar-nav__note, such as the repository and runner in use.
The component needs no script. The app sets aria-current on the right link when the screen changes.

components.name: skeleton
components.title: Skeleton
components.purpose: Plain shapes that stand where content is about to appear, so the page keeps its layout while it loads.
whenToUse: While a list, a description or a block of content is fetched, when its shape is known and it usually arrives within a few seconds.
On the first load of a view. The shapes match what will replace them: as many rows as usually show, lines the length of the text.
whenNotToUse: When the shape of what is coming is not known, or the wait is an action the reader started. Use a spinner, with text that says what is happening.
When the wait has a measurable length, such as 7 of 12 checks. Use progress.
Together with a spinner for the same wait. Use one of the two.
After the fetch has failed, or after about ten seconds. Replace it with an error state that says what to do: a skeleton that never resolves is a broken promise.
While content already on screen is refreshed. Keep the content and set aria-busy on its container.
For text that is streaming in. Use streaming.

variants.name: line
variants.use: A bar 12px tall in the space of one line of text, as wide as its container. For a paragraph or a set of facts, one above the other.

variants.name: medium line
variants.use: With gw-skeleton__line: 60% of the width, for a title or the last line of a paragraph.

variants.name: short line
variants.use: With gw-skeleton__line: 35% of the width, for a label, a branch name or a time.

variants.name: row
variants.use: A list row at least 44px tall, holding one or two lines. Its container also takes gw-skeleton--rows, so the rows touch and are divided by a rule, as list rows are.

variants.name: block
variants.use: A rectangle 132px tall and as wide as its container, for a code block or a diff.

accessibility: The container is a div with the gw-skeleton class and aria-busy="true". Its first child is a span with the gw-visually-hidden class that says what is loading, such as Loading tasks. The shapes are empty span elements and are not read out.

When the content arrives, the app replaces the whole container with it. Nothing of the skeleton stays, so aria-busy goes with it. When the skeleton stands inside a region that stays, such as a section with a heading, put aria-busy on that region and remove it when the content arrives.
When the fetch fails, or has taken about ten seconds, the app replaces the container with an error state that says what happened and offers Retry.
The shapes fade slowly between full and partial strength. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the animation is off and the shapes hold still.
A skeleton has no controls and takes no focus. If the content it replaces had focus, move focus to the view's heading until the content is back.
The component needs no script beyond the app swapping it for the content.

components.name: switch
components.title: Switch
components.purpose: An on-or-off setting that takes effect as soon as it changes.
whenToUse: For a setting the app saves the moment it changes, such as Notify me when a run needs approval.
In a list of settings, one switch per row, each with its own label.
whenNotToUse: In a form that is sent with a button. Use a checkbox, which is read as part of the form.
To choose between two named options, such as Unified and Split. Use a segmented control.
To start or stop something that takes time or cannot be undone, such as cancelling a run. Use a button.
To show or hide part of the view from a toolbar. Use an icon button with aria-pressed.
accessibility: Use input type="checkbox" with role="switch" and gw-switch__input, and a label with gw-switch__label whose for attribute is the input's id. A screen reader announces the label, the switch role and on or off.
Inside the div with gw-switch the order is: the label, the state text, the input, then the description and the error if there are any.

The state text is a span with gw-switch__state and aria-hidden="true", holding two spans: gw-switch__on with the word On and gw-switch__off with the word Off. The stylesheet shows the one that matches the input, so no script changes the text. It is hidden from assistive technology because the switch role already says on or off. Always include it: with the thumb's position, it is what keeps the state from resting on colour.
The label names the setting and does not change with the state. Write it so that On means the thing in the label happens.
A description is a p with gw-switch__description, linked from the input with aria-describedby.

components.name: tabs
components.title: Tabs
components.purpose: A row of tabs that switches between panels of one view, showing one panel at a time.
whenToUse: For two to seven panels that belong to one thing, such as the summary, diff and log of a run, when the reader looks at one at a time.
Wrapped in the gw-tabs element from behaviors/groundwork.js, which handles selection and the arrow keys.
On a plain div with the same classes when the app, such as a React app, sets aria-selected, tabindex and hidden itself.
whenNotToUse: For moving between screens. Use the tab bar below 768px and the sidebar nav at 768px and up, with links and aria-current.
For sections the reader may want open together or scan in one pass. Use an accordion or plain headings.
For a choice that changes a setting or filters a list. Use a select.
For one panel. Show the content with no tabs.

sizes.name: default

accessibility: Markup: a gw-tabs element (or a div) with the gw-tabs class holds one gw-tabs__list with role="tablist" and an aria-label, then one gw-tabs__panel per tab.

Each tab is a button with type="button", role="tab", an id, and aria-controls naming its panel. Each panel has role="tabpanel", an id, aria-labelledby naming its tab, and tabindex="0" so a panel of plain text can take focus.

Write the first state in the markup: aria-selected="true" on one tab and "false" on the rest, and the hidden attribute on every panel but the selected one. The page is then right before any script runs.

What gw-tabs does: on connection and on every selection it sets aria-selected on each tab, tabindex="0" on the selected tab and "-1" on the others, and hidden on every panel except the one the selected tab controls. A click selects a tab. It sets no class and no inline style.

Keyboard, with gw-tabs: Tab moves into the row onto the selected tab, and Tab again moves to the panel. Left and Right move to the previous and next tab and select it, wrapping at the ends. Home selects the first tab and End the last.
Without gw-tabs the app does the same: it sets those three attributes and handles click, Left, Right, Home and End. Nothing else is needed for the styles.
The selected tab is marked by a bar and a heavier label as well as by colour. Never mark it with a class.
Load behaviors/groundwork.js once as a module: <script type="module" src="behaviors/groundwork.js"></script>. Loading it twice is harmless.
While a panel is fetched, set aria-busy="true" on it and show a spinner with text. When the fetch fails, put an alert in the panel that says what to do.
Keep labels to one or two words. A label is never cut: the row scrolls instead, and a tab that takes focus is scrolled into view.

components.name: timeline
components.title: Timeline
components.purpose: Events in the order they happened, each with its time, who acted and what happened, joined by a rail.
whenToUse: For the history of one run, task or approval: who did what, and when.
For a run in progress, with the step it is on now marked as the current one.
With the dense variant for a long log of short events.
whenNotToUse: For the messages of a conversation with an agent. Use message rows in a transcript.
For steps the reader has yet to take, such as a setup wizard. This component records what happened.
For a set of things in no particular order. Use the list.
For events compared across columns, or filtered and sorted. Use the data table.
When there are no events, while the first fetch runs or after it fails. Put an empty state, a spinner or an error state in place of the list. Never render an ol with no items.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Time and actor on one line, what happened on the next, 16px between events.

variants.name: dense
variants.use: 8px between events, with what happened on the same line as the time and actor where there is room.

accessibility: Use an ol with one li, gw-timeline__item, for each event, oldest first unless the view says otherwise. A screen reader announces the count and the position.

Each item holds a p with the class gw-timeline__meta and then a p with the class gw-timeline__event. The meta line holds a time element, gw-timeline__time, with a datetime attribute, and the actor, gw-timeline__actor, in words. The event line says what happened as a sentence fragment that starts with a verb.
Write the time so it cannot be misread: the clock time for events of one day, the date as well when the list spans days.

Mark the current step with aria-current="step" on its li and with words in a span of the class gw-timeline__current at the end of the meta line, such as Current step. The filled mark only supports the words.
The rail and the marks are drawn by the stylesheet and are decoration. Nothing is said by them alone.

A long timeline pairs with show-more: render the most recent events, twenty or so, and put one secondary button after the list whose label gives the count, such as Show 34 earlier events. On press the app adds the items to the same ol and moves focus to the first one added. The button is outside the ol.
When an event is added while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the list.
The timeline has no controls of its own and needs no script.

components.name: toast
components.title: Toast
components.purpose: A brief status message that appears at the edge of the screen without taking focus and leaves by itself.
whenToUse: To confirm that something the reader just did has happened, such as a copy or a push.
To report a passing event from elsewhere in the app, such as a run that started, with at most one action.
whenNotToUse: For an action the reader may want to take back. Use the undo toast.
For a failure the reader must act on, or a result that should stay on screen. Use an alert in the view.
For a mistake in a form control. Use the field's error.
For a state of the whole app, such as a lost connection. Use a banner.
For a question. Use a dialog.

variants.name: info
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. A passing event. The label reads Note.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Something the reader asked for has happened. The label reads Done.

variants.name: danger
variants.use: Something failed and the reader loses nothing by missing the message, or can try again with its one action. The label reads Error.

accessibility: Put one region in the page from the start, as the last element in the body, empty: a div with the class gw-toast__region, role="status", aria-live="polite" and aria-atomic="false". A screen reader announces only what is added to a live region that already exists.

The app shows a toast by appending a gw-toast element to the region and hides it by removing that element. Append the newest last. The stylesheet shows the last three and hides any before them, so remove the oldest when a fourth arrives.
A toast never takes focus. It is announced when the reader's screen reader is next idle.

Each message starts with gw-toast__label holding the tone in words: Note, Done or Error, then a colon. The tone's icon is drawn by the stylesheet. The message is one sentence, and an error says what to do.
A toast has at most one action, a button with gw-button gw-button--small gw-toast__action after the message. Nothing may be reachable only from a toast: the same action is somewhere in the view.

How long it stays is the app's timer: remove a toast without an action after 5 seconds, and one with an action after 10 seconds. Pause the timer while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it, and while the page is hidden. Do not remove a danger toast on a timer shorter than 10 seconds.

The region is fixed to the bottom of the screen on a phone and to the bottom trailing corner at 768px and wider, above the page and below nothing but a modal dialog. While a modal dialog is open the page behind it is inert, so report the result of a dialog's action after it closes.
